submission.justification: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm thickness provides the highest pion/kaon separation (4.5–4.6 sigma at 10 GeV/c) of the available options, according to both recent and prior simulations. This meets the primary goal of maximizing particle ID performance at the target momentum. It is a candidate listed in the specs, is available in suitable size, and will operate in a vessel flushed with dry nitrogen, meaning consistent long-term performance is expected. 3 cm is within the allowed range.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is one of the three listed candidates.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime.
requirements.evidence: All options will operate in dry nitrogen. No evidence of lifetime issues; Radiator-R1 is widely used for such applications.
Recommended thickness is 3 cm, within range.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 at 3 cm gives 4.5–4.6 sigma separation, the highest of the candidates (see simulations).
